# UX and Monetization Improvements Design

**Date:** 2026-08-27
**Status:** Approved for implementation

## Overview

Six targeted improvements to chat quality, paywall UX, gallery access, and analytics.

---

## Item 1: Anti-Refusal Hardening for Image Teaser

**Problem:** When a user requests a photo in chat, the image IS generated successfully, but the in-character text response generated by `generateImageTeaser()` sometimes says the character cannot provide an image (LLM refusal slip-through).

**Fix location:** `backend/src/chat/image-turn.ts` - `generateImageTeaser()`

**Changes:**
1. Strengthen the system prompt with an explicit hard rule appended to the existing text:
   ```
   CRITICAL: Never say you cannot, will not, or are unable to provide, send, or show an image. You ARE sending one right now. Any refusal breaks the experience.
   ```
2. Post-LLM refusal scanner: after receiving the LLM response, check for refusal patterns. If found, replace with the deterministic fallback.

**Refusal patterns to detect (case-insensitive):**
- `cannot`, `can't`, `unable to`, `don't have the ability`, `I'm an AI`, `I am an AI`, `not able to`, `can not`, `won't be able`

---

## Item 2: Video Intent Detection and In-Character Redirect

**Problem:** The chat input has a "Video" quick-action button. Users can also type free-text video requests. Currently both routes through the image pipeline (the image keyword pattern matches `video|clip|vid`). We want to remove the button and intercept video intent to return a gentle in-character redirect instead of generating media.

**Changes:**

`backend/src/chat/intent.ts`:
- Extend `MessageIntent` type to `"image" | "text" | "video_request"`
- Add `VIDEO_KEYWORD_PATTERNS` checked BEFORE image patterns (so video requests don't fall into image generation)
- Video patterns: `video`, `clip`, `vid`, `film me`, `movie`, `short film`
- Add `matchVideoKeyword(text)` export

`backend/src/http/chat-stream.ts`:
- Before the image intent check, check for `video_request`
- If video_request: persist user message, generate in-character redirect text (via `callLLM` with a short system prompt), stream it as a normal text response, persist assistant message, emit `done`. No image generated, no token spent on image quota.
- In-character redirect system prompt: `"You are ${characterName}. The user asked for a video. Warmly and charmingly let them know you can't do videos right now, but you'd love to send them photos and keep chatting. 1-2 sentences, flirtatious and in-character. No hashtags, no emojis, no stage directions."`
- Fallback text (if LLM fails): `"Videos aren't my thing just yet, but I'd love to send you a photo instead — just ask!"`

`frontend/components/chat/ChatWindow.tsx`:
- Delete the Video `SceneButton` block (lines 735-742)
- Keep the Photo `SceneButton`
- The label "Show me the scene:" can stay or be removed (keep it for now since Photo button remains)

## Item 3: PaywallModal Character Image (Two-Prop Fix)

**Problem:** `PaywallModal` already has `avatarUrl` and `characterName` props and the rendering logic for the character image background, but `ChatWindow` never passes them.

**Fix:** In `ChatWindow.tsx` at the `<PaywallModal ...>` call, add:
```tsx
avatarUrl={avatarUrl}
characterName={characterName}
```
Both values are already in scope in `ChatWindow`.

---

## Item 4: Global Quota Pre-Check on Character Mount

**Problem:** Message and image quotas are enforced globally (per user, not per character). But when a user switches characters, `ChatWindow` mounts fresh with `paywall = null`. The user can type and attempt to send before the server returns a 402. The paywall should appear immediately on mount if quota is already exhausted.

**Fix:** In `ChatWindow.tsx`, add a `useEffect` that runs on mount (empty dependency array). It calls `GET /api/billing/status` (the existing Next.js proxy route at `frontend/app/api/billing/status/route.ts`). If `entitlements.chats.remaining === 0` (free or paid quota) or `entitlements.images.remaining === 0`, pre-populate `paywall` state immediately.

The paywall state needs to be constructed from the entitlements response shape:
```ts
setPaywall({
  scope: ent.active ? "plan_quota" : "free_trial",
  kind: "chat",
  used: ent.chats.used,
  limit: ent.chats.limit,
  plans: [],   // PaywallModal fetches live plans on its own mount
})
```

## Item 5: Persistent Gallery Image Unlock

**Problem:** Subscribed users' image quota (100-300 images depending on plan) can only be spent generating new chat images. Locked character gallery images are inaccessible regardless of remaining quota. Users should be able to "spend" 1 image token to permanently unlock a gallery image.

### Database Schema

New model in `schema.prisma`:
```prisma
model UserUnlockedMedia {
  id              String   @id @default(uuid())
  userId          String
  characterMediaId String
  unlockedAt      DateTime @default(now())

  @@unique([userId, characterMediaId])
  @@index([userId])
}
```

New `TokenReason` enum value: `gallery_unlock`

### Backend API

`POST /gallery/unlock` (new file `backend/src/http/gallery.ts`):
- Auth-gated (401 if no session)
- Body: `{ characterMediaId: string }` (Zod-validated)
- Logic:
  1. Call `assertCanImage(userId)` - throws 402 PaywallError if no quota
  2. Upsert `UserUnlockedMedia` (idempotent - if already unlocked, skip token deduction)
  3. If newly unlocked (created, not updated): call `recordImageConsumption(userId)`
  4. Return `{ success: true }`
- Register in `backend/src/index.ts` as `handleGalleryRoute`

### Frontend Changes

**PrivateContentGallery (`/private-content/[characterId]/page.tsx` + component):**
- Server page queries `UserUnlockedMedia` for `{ userId, characterMediaId: { in: lockedMedia.map(m => m.id) } }`
- Signs URLs for already-unlocked images
- Passes to component: `unlockedTiles: { id, url }[]`, `lockedTiles: { id, blur }[]`, `hasActivePlan: boolean`, `characterId`
- `PrivateContentGallery` becomes a client component
- Unlocked tiles: render real image
- Locked tiles with `hasActivePlan`: render blur + "1 token" badge on hover; on click call `POST /gallery/unlock`, on success call `router.refresh()` (server re-signs the now-unlocked URL)
- Locked tiles without active plan: `<Link href="/billing">` (existing behavior)

**GalleryPaywall (chat sidebar `GalleryPaywall.tsx`):**
- Parent (`chat/[characterId]/page.tsx`) queries `UserUnlockedMedia` + checks active subscription
- New props: `mediaIds: string[]` (parallel to `images`), `unlockedMediaIds: string[]`, `hasActivePlan: boolean`
- For index i > 0:
  - If `unlockedMediaIds.includes(mediaIds[i])`: show `images[i]` (URL already in props, just wasn't displayed)
  - If `hasActivePlan` and not unlocked: "1 token" badge; on click call `POST /gallery/unlock`, on success set `images[i]` visible in local state
  - If no active plan: existing lock overlay + UpgradeModal

## Item 6: CTA Click Tracking

**Problem:** No tracking of which users click which upgrade/payment buttons, where, or how often. This data is needed for conversion analysis.

### Architecture

Reuse the existing `AnalyticsEvent` table and `track()` utility. No new DB table.

**Shared (`packages/shared/src/analytics.ts`):**
- Add `"cta_click"` to `AnalyticsEventName` union

**Backend (`backend/src/http/analytics.ts` - new file):**
- `POST /analytics/cta` (auth-gated)
- Body: `{ buttonId: string, area: string, path: string }` (Zod-validated)
- Calls `track("cta_click", { buttonId, area, path }, userId)`
- Returns `204` always (fire-and-forget; never blocks UI)
- Register in `backend/src/index.ts` as `handleAnalyticsRoute`

**Frontend (`frontend/lib/track-cta.ts` - new file):**
```ts
export function trackCta(buttonId: string, area: string): void {
  void fetch(`${BACKEND_URL}/analytics/cta`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    credentials: "include",
    body: JSON.stringify({ buttonId, area, path: window.location.pathname }),
  }).catch(() => {});  // fire-and-forget, never throws
}
```

**Button IDs and areas to instrument:**

| Component | Button ID | Area |
|---|---|---|
| `PaywallModal.tsx` | `paywall_daily_pass` | `paywall_modal` |
| `PaywallModal.tsx` | `paywall_weekly_pass` | `paywall_modal` |
| `PaywallModal.tsx` | `paywall_monthly_pass` | `paywall_modal` |
| `PaywallModal.tsx` | `paywall_buy_tokens` | `paywall_modal` |
| `GalleryPaywall.tsx` | `gallery_upgrade` | `gallery_sidebar` |
| `GalleryPaywall.tsx` | `gallery_unlock_image` | `gallery_sidebar` |
| `PrivateContentGallery.tsx` | `gallery_unlock_image` | `private_gallery` |
| `PrivateContentGallery.tsx` | `gallery_upgrade` | `private_gallery` |
| `BillingClient.tsx` | `billing_sub_monthly` | `billing_page` |
| `BillingClient.tsx` | `billing_sub_yearly` | `billing_page` |
| `BillingClient.tsx` | `billing_pack_100` | `billing_page` |
| `BillingClient.tsx` | `billing_pack_500` | `billing_page` |

## Global Constraints

- No em dashes anywhere (code, comments, docs, commit messages)
- TypeScript strict mode; no `any` without annotation comment
- Zod validates all route handler bodies at trust boundary
- `import { prisma } from "@buttercupp/database"` - never `new PrismaClient()`
- No git commit, push, or deploy without explicit human approval
- `POPPY_DEV_BYPASS_PAYWALL=true` in `backend/.env` for local dev only
- No new columns or tables without a Prisma migration (`prisma migrate dev`)
- `AnalyticsEventName` type is in `packages/shared/src/analytics.ts` - always add new names there, never inline strings
